questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **BODMAS** rule by grouping addition and subtraction for faster calculation.

⇒ 91 + 32 − 28 + (65 × 2) − (42 + 19)

⇒ (123 − 28) + 130 − 61

⇒ 95 + 130 − 61 = 164

**∴ The correct answer is 164.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 91 + 32 − 28 + 65 × 2 − (42 + 19)

**Formula Used:** **VBODMAS** Rule (Vinculum, Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

⇒ 91 + 32 − 28 + 65 × 2 − **61** (Solving the bracket: 42 + 19 = 61)

⇒ 91 + 32 − 28 + **130** − 61 (Solving the multiplication: 65 × 2 = 130)

⇒ **123** − 28 + 130 − 61 (Performing addition: 91 + 32 = 123)

⇒ **95** + 130 − 61 (Performing subtraction: 123 − 28 = 95)

⇒ **225** − 61 (Performing addition: 95 + 130 = 225)

⇒ 164 (Performing final subtraction: 225 − 61 = 164)

**∴ The correct answer is 164.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It is a mnemonic to help remember the order of operations: **Brackets**, **Orders** (powers/roots), **Division**, **Multiplication**, **Addition**, and **Subtraction**.

Sign Rules

When performing operations, remember that (+) × (−) = (−) and (−) × (−) = (+). In addition, the sign of the number with the larger absolute value is kept.

Priority of Addition and Subtraction

Addition and subtraction have the same priority level and are generally solved from **left to right** in an expression.

questions.question: 79 + 36 - 44 + 18 of 1 + (33 ÷ 3) + 27 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve the **bracket** and **of** operations first: (33 ÷ 3) = 11 and 18 of 1 = 18.

The expression becomes: 79 + 36 − 44 + 18 + 11 + 27.

Group all positive numbers: 79 + 36 + 18 + 11 + 27 = 171.

Subtract the remaining value: 171 − 44 = 127.

**∴ The correct answer is 127.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 79 + 36 − 44 + 18 of 1 + (33 ÷ 3) + 27

To solve this, apply the **BODMAS** rule (Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

⇒ 79 + 36 − 44 + 18 of 1 + 11 + 27

⇒ 79 + 36 − 44 + 18 + 11 + 27

⇒ 115 − 44 + 18 + 11 + 27

⇒ 71 + 18 + 11 + 27

⇒ 89 + 11 + 27

⇒ 100 + 27

⇒ 127

**∴ The correct answer is 127.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the order of operations: **B**rackets, **O**f, **D**ivision, **M**ultiplication, **A**ddition, and then **S**ubtraction.

Of Operator

The word **'of'** acts as a multiplication operator but it must be calculated before any **division** or **multiplication** signs.

Bracket Sequence

Solve in the order: small brackets ( ), then curly brackets { }, and finally square brackets [ ].

questions.question: Two numbers are such that their HCF is 18 and their LCM is 540. If one of the numbers is 90, find the other number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Product of **two numbers** = **HCF × LCM**

Other number = (**18 × 540**) ÷ **90**

Other number = 18 × (540 ÷ 90) = 18 × 6

Other number = 108

**∴ The correct answer is 108.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**HCF** of two numbers = 18

**LCM** of two numbers = 540

**First number** (a) = 90

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers (a × b) = **HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/66cb4350df0fa8dd88e4cd3b6427aab34b1c766c8339b6788e994ae46f075875.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the other number be **b**.

⇒ 90 × b = 18 × 540

⇒ 90 × b = 9720

⇒ b = 9720 ÷ 90

⇒ b = 108

**∴ The correct answer is 108.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF and LCM Property

For any two positive integers **a** and **b**, the product of the numbers is always equal to the product of their **HCF** and **LCM**: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

HCF as a Factor

The **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** of a set of numbers is always a **divisor** or factor of their **Least Common Multiple (LCM)**.

Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are **co-prime** (their HCF is 1), then their **LCM** is simply the **product** of the two numbers.

questions.question: ((0.7)⁴ - (0.3)⁴)/((0.7)² + (0.3)²) = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **algebraic identity**: a⁴ − b⁴ = (a² − b²)(a² + b²).

The given expression simplifies to: **a² − b²**.

Here, a = 0.7 and b = 0.3.

Calculation: (0.7)² − (0.3)² = 0.49 − 0.09 = 0.40.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: ((0.7)⁴ − (0.3)⁴) / ((0.7)² + (0.3)²)

**Formula Used:**

**Difference of squares**: (x² − y²) = (x − y)(x + y)

Applying this to **a⁴ − b⁴** by treating x = a² and y = b²:

a⁴ − b⁴ = (a²)² − (b²)² = (a² − b²)(a² + b²)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let a = 0.7 and b = 0.3

⇒ Expression = [(a² − b²)(a² + b²)] / (a² + b²)

⇒ Expression = a² − b²

⇒ (0.7)² − (0.3)²

⇒ 0.49 − 0.09

⇒ 0.40

**∴ The correct answer is 0.40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities

Basic identities like (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b² are frequently used to simplify high-power **polynomial expressions** quickly.

Higher Power Reductions

For even powers, always look for the form (aⁿ)² − (bⁿ)² to factorize the numerator and cancel common terms in the **denominator**.

BODMAS Rule

Always prioritize **Brackets** and **Exponents** before performing division or subtraction in complex numerical simplifications.

questions.question: (1)/(4+sqrt{2)}+(1)/(4-sqrt{2)}=?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ For an expression of the form 1/(a + √b) + 1/(a − √b), the result is always **2a / (a² − b)**. Here, a = 4 and b = 2. Result = (2 × 4) / (4² − 2) = 8 / (16 − 2) = 8 / 14 = 4/7. **∴ The correct answer is 4/7.**

questions.question: sqrt{108900 + sqrt{12321}} = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the individual square roots using simple visual observation:

⇒ **√12321** = 111 (using the standard palindromic pattern where 111² = 12321)

⇒ **√108900** = 330 (since 33² = 1089 and the square root of two trailing zeros is one zero)

⇒ Substituting these values: √(330 + 111) = √441 = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = √(√108900 + √12321)

**Calculation:**

First, calculate the value of the inner square roots:

⇒ Let x = √12321

⇒ x = 111

⇒ Let y = √108900

⇒ y = 330

Now, substitute the values of x and y back into the main expression:

⇒ Required value = √(y + x)

⇒ Required value = √(330 + 111)

⇒ Required value = √441

⇒ Required value = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Square Root of Palindromic Numbers

For numbers consisting of digits that increase sequentially up to a peak and then decrease (e.g., 121, 12321, 1234321), the square root contains only 1s, where the count of 1s equals the peak digit. Thus, √12321 = 111.

Square Root of Numbers with Trailing Zeros

When finding the square root of a perfect square ending in an even number of zeros, the square root contains exactly half as many zeros at the end. For example, √108900 = √1089 × √100 = 33 × 10 = 330.

Simplification Hierarchy

In mathematical expressions involving nested radicals, always simplify the innermost operations first before proceeding outward to the main radical.

questions.question: There is a rectangular garden of 150 metres × 60 metres. A path of width 2 metres is build outside the garden. What is the area (in square metre) of the path?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **area of a path** built **outside** a rectangle, use the formula:

**Area = 2w(L + B + 2w)**

Where **L** = 150 m, **B** = 60 m, and **w** = 2 m.

Area = 2 × 2 × (150 + 60 + 2 × 2) = 4 × (210 + 4) = 4 × 214 = 856 m².

**∴ The correct answer is 856 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6fd783123297f3b0a51bd9c104f82131538cfd3fb1e0b17411b1fa1cb57934c7.png] 

**Given:**

⇒ **Length of garden (L)** = 150 m

⇒ **Breadth of garden (B)** = 60 m

⇒ **Width of path (w)** = 2 m

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since the path is outside, **Outer Length** = 150 + 2 + 2 = 154 m

⇒ **Outer Breadth** = 60 + 2 + 2 = 64 m

⇒ **Area of Path** = (Outer Length × Outer Breadth) − (Inner Length × Inner Breadth)

⇒ Area = (154 × 64) − (150 × 60)

⇒ Area = 9856 − 9000

⇒ Area = 856 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 856 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Path Inside a Rectangle

If the path is built inside the rectangular garden, the formula becomes Area = 2w(L + B − 2w).

Central Cross Paths

Area of two paths crossing each other at the center of a rectangle is given by Area = w(L + B − w).

Circular Path

The area of a circular path around a circle with radius 'r' and width 'w' is π((r+w)² − r²) = πw(2r + w).

questions.question: 1² + 2² + 3² ..... + 30² = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The sum of the squares of the first **n natural numbers** is calculated using the direct formula: [n × (n + 1) × (2n + 1)] / 6.

For **n = 30**, the sum is (30 × 31 × 61) / 6.

On simplifying: 5 × 31 × 61 = 155 × 61 = 9455.

**∴ The correct answer is 9455.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The series is the sum of squares of the first **30 natural numbers**: 1² + 2² + 3² + ... + 30².

**Formula Used:** Sum (Sₙ) = [n(n + 1)(2n + 1)] / 6

⇒ Here, the total number of terms **n = 30**.

⇒ S₃₀ = [30 × (30 + 1) × (2 × 30 + 1)] / 6

⇒ S₃₀ = [30 × 31 × 61] / 6

⇒ S₃₀ = 5 × 31 × 61

⇒ S₃₀ = 155 × 61

⇒ S₃₀ = 9455

**∴ The correct answer is 9455.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of First n Natural Numbers

The sum of the first **n** natural numbers (1 + 2 + 3 + ... + n) is given by the formula: **[n(n + 1)] / 2**.

Sum of Cubes of First n Natural Numbers

The sum of the cubes of the first **n** natural numbers (1³ + 2³ + ... + n³) is given by: **[[n(n + 1)] / 2]²**.

Sum of First n Odd Numbers

The sum of the first **n** odd natural numbers (1 + 3 + 5 + ... up to n terms) is equal to **n²**.

questions.question: Sum of the diagonals of a rhombus is 42 cm. Side of the rhombus is 15 cm. What is the area (in square cm) of the rhombus?

Identify the **Pythagorean triplet** for the right triangle formed by half-diagonals and the **side (15 cm)**: **9, 12, 15**.

Check **sum of diagonals**: (2 × 9) + (2 × 12) = 18 + 24 = **42 cm** (Matches given condition).

Diagonals are **18 cm** and **24 cm**.

Area = (18 × 24) ÷ 2 = 216 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 216 cm².**

questions.question: A new student having weight 40 kg join a class of 39 students. The average weight of the class reduces by 0.5 kg. What is the new average weight (in kg) of the class?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**New Average** = **New Weight** + (**Initial Students** × **Reduction**)

⇒ **New Average** = 40 + (39 × 0.5)

⇒ **New Average** = 40 + 19.5

⇒ **New Average** = 59.5 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 59.5 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial students = 39

Weight of new student = 40 kg

Reduction in average = 0.5 kg

**Formula Used:**

Average = Total Sum of Observations ÷ Number of Observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cfa1fd2e4eb2e14079e48b4432412a528666ba5b956043d7ede0fedba1defc28.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **initial average weight** of the 39 students be **x** kg.

⇒ Total weight of 39 students = 39 × x = 39x

⇒ Total weight of 40 students (including the new student) = 39x + 40

⇒ New average weight = **x − 0.5**

⇒ **New Average** = (Total weight of 40 students) ÷ 40

⇒ x − 0.5 = (39x + 40) ÷ 40

⇒ 40 × (x − 0.5) = 39x + 40

⇒ 40x − 20 = 39x + 40

⇒ 40x − 39x = 40 + 20

⇒ x = 60 kg (Old Average)

⇒ **New Average weight** = 60 − 0.5 = 59.5 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 59.5 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Deviation Method

The sum of deviations of all observations from their average is always zero. New member weight − Old average = Total members × Change in average.

Weighted Average Formula

Weighted Average = (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the count and x is the individual average/value.

Inclusion/Exclusion Rule

When a new person joins, New Value = New Average + Initial Number × (Change in Average). If the average decreases, the change is considered positive in this specific adjustment format.

questions.question: Average of some numbers is 'p'. 22 is the smallest number among these numbers. Which of the following statement will be always correct? I. p = 35. II. 50 will be the largest number among these numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Average (p)** of a set of numbers must always satisfy the condition: **Smallest Number ≤ p ≤ Largest Number**.

Given the **Smallest number** is 22, the **Average (p)** can be any value greater than or equal to 22, and the **Largest number** can be any value greater than or equal to 22.

Statement I claims **p** is exactly 35, which is not mandatory.

Statement II claims the **Largest number** is exactly 50, which is also not mandatory.

Since both are specific cases and not universal rules, neither is always correct.

**∴ The correct answer is Neither I nor II.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: **Smallest number** = 22, **Average** = p.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f7f4d3e9419b059fcdee305552a3e8ca9529af2ea8cb1c7bc3aebd64e5cad1aa.png] 

⇒ Let the set of numbers be {22, 23}. Here, **Average (p)** = 22.5 and **Largest** = 23. (Both I and II are False)

⇒ Let the set of numbers be {22, 48}. Here, **Average (p)** = 35 and **Largest** = 48. (Statement II is False)

⇒ Let the set of numbers be {22, 22, 106}. Here, **Average (p)** = 50 and **Largest** = 106. (Statement I is False)

⇒ Since we can find instances where these statements do not hold, they are not **always correct**.

**∴ The correct answer is Neither I nor II.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Range Property of Average

The average of any data set must lie strictly between (or equal to) the minimum and maximum values of the set: **xₘᵢₙ ≤ Average ≤ xₘₐₓ**.

Sum of Deviations

The algebraic sum of the deviations of a set of observations from their **Arithmetic Mean** is always zero: **Σ(xᵢ − p) = 0**.

Effect of Change in Origin

If a constant **k** is added to or subtracted from every term in a set, the new average will be **p ± k**.

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 7 : 9 and their Highest Common Factor is 3. What are the two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If the **ratio** of two numbers is a : b and their **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** is H, then the numbers are (a × H) and (b × H).

Given **Ratio** = 7 : 9 and **HCF** = 3.

Numbers = (7 × 3) and (9 × 3) = 21 and 27.

**∴ The correct answer is 21, 27.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Ratio** of numbers = 7 : 9 and their **HCF** = 3.

**Formula Used:** Number = Ratio Unit × HCF

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/82a841be72a593dc21c2b5eb546565027455b8499b6c55ec9d1555ae25862a54.png] 

⇒ Let the two numbers be **7x** and **9x**.

⇒ The **HCF** of 7x and 9x is **x** (since 7 and 9 are **co-prime** numbers).

⇒ According to the question, **HCF = 3**.

⇒ Therefore, **x = 3**.

⇒ First number = 7 × 3 = **21**.

⇒ Second number = 9 × 3 = **27**.

**∴ The correct answer is 21, 27.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Relation

For any two numbers, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their **HCF** and **LCM**. Formula: **HCF × LCM = n₁ × n₂**.

LCM from HCF and Ratio

If the ratio of two numbers is **x : y** and their **HCF** is **H**, then their **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** is given by **LCM = x × y × H**.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are called **co-prime** if their **Highest Common Factor** is **1**. In a simplified ratio a : b, a and b are always co-prime.

questions.question: Element A is 16 percent by weight in a mixture. How much mixture is required to obtain 64 kg of element A?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct relation: 16% of **total mixture** = 64 kg

Divide by 16 to find 1%: 1% of **mixture** = 64 ÷ 16 = 4 kg

Multiply by 100 for 100%: **Total mixture** = 4 × 100 = 400 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 400 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Weight of **Element A** = 64 kg, **Percentage** of Element A in the mixture = 16%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9851438eed9c382e1fcc52455532e7cb786bebb4d68f2784796048d9c237fa85.png] 

⇒ Let the total weight of the **mixture** be X kg.

⇒ 16% of X = 64

⇒ (16 ÷ 100) × X = 64

⇒ X = (64 × 100) ÷ 16

⇒ X = 4 × 100

⇒ X = 400 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 400 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mass Percentage Formula

Concentration of a substance = (Mass of substance ÷ Total mass of mixture) × 100

Ratio Method for Mixtures

16% can be written as 4:25 (Part:Total). If 4 units represent 64 kg, then 1 unit is 16 kg, making 25 units equal to 400 kg.

Finding Total from Percentage Change

Total Value = Given Value ÷ Percentage Fraction (e.g., Total = 64 ÷ 0.16 = 400 kg).

questions.question: Ratio of the cost price of an article to the selling price of the article is 5 : 2. Loss is Rs. 300. What is the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **ratio** of **Cost Price** (CP) to **Selling Price** (SP) is 5 : 2.

**Loss units** = CP − SP = 5 − 2 = 3 units.

Given, 3 units = ₹300 → 1 unit = ₹100.

**Cost Price** = 5 units = 5 × ₹100 = ₹500.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹500.**

questions.question: Ratio of the cost price of an article to the selling price of the article is 10 : 13. What will be the ratio of the value of profit to the cost price of the article?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Given **Cost Price (CP)** : **Selling Price (SP)** = 10 : 13 Directly take **CP** = 10 units and **SP** = 13 units. **Profit** = 13 − 10 = 3 units. Required Ratio (**Profit : CP**) = 3 : 10. **∴ The correct answer is 3 : 10.**

questions.question: An interval of 8 hours 20 minutes is wrongly estimated as 8 hours 40 minutes. What is the error percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert values to a common unit: **Actual time** = 500 min and **Estimated time** = 520 min.

Absolute **Error** = 520 − 500 = 20 min.

**Error percentage** = (Error ÷ Actual Value) × 100.

Error % = (20 ÷ 500) × 100 = 4%.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Actual time interval = 8 hr 20 min

Estimated time interval = 8 hr 40 min

**Formula Used:**

Error Percentage = (Absolute Error ÷ Actual Value) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/df548a0d32df6a4eff21b4ffc17db8de298fa956c02dc56585e443c2238bfc3d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Actual time in minutes = (8 × 60) + 20 = 480 + 20 = 500 min

⇒ Estimated time in minutes = (8 × 60) + 40 = 480 + 40 = 520 min

⇒ Absolute Error = 520 − 500 = 20 min

⇒ Error Percentage = (20 ÷ 500) × 100

⇒ Error Percentage = 2000 ÷ 500 = 4%

**∴ The correct answer is 4 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Absolute Error

It is the numerical difference between the **measured value** and the **actual value**: |Measured − Actual|.

Relative Error

It is the ratio of the **absolute error** to the **actual value**. It expresses how large the error is relative to the total size.

Percentage Change

The formula for **percentage increase** or **decrease** is always calculated on the **original (base) value**: (Change ÷ Original Value) × 100.

questions.question: A pipe can empty 1/5 part of a tank in 36 minutes. In how much time (in minutes) will it empty the complete tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In fraction-based problems, the **Total Work** is represented by the **denominator**.

If **1 unit** (out of 5) takes **36 min** to empty,

Then **5 units** (complete tank) will take 36 × 5 = **180 min**.

**∴ The correct answer is 180 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Part of the tank emptied = **1/5**

Time taken to empty this part = **36 minutes**

**Formula Used:**

Total Time = (Time Taken) ÷ (Part Emptied)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3190c0f592c52d548db79d11302a1cfd76e70923bb427e16a37429240f659051.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **total capacity** of the tank be 1 unit.

⇒ Time taken to empty 1/5 part = 36 min

⇒ Time taken to empty 1 unit = 36 ÷ (1/5)

⇒ Total Time = 36 × 5

⇒ Total Time = 180 min

**∴ The correct answer is 180 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Rule

If a pipe can empty a tank in **x** hours, then the part emptied in 1 hour is **1/x**.

Unitary Method in Fractions

If **a/b** part of a work is done in **T** time, then the whole work is done in **T × (b/a)** time.

Efficiency and Time

The **Efficiency** of a pipe is inversely proportional to the **Time** taken to complete the work (filling or emptying).

questions.question: A alone can do a work in 15 days. B alone can do the same work in 25 days. C alone can do the same work in 50 days. They started the work together. A and B both the left the work after 5 days. In how many days can C complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work (LCM of 15, 25, 50) = 150 units.

Combined efficiency of **A**, **B**, and **C** = 10 + 6 + 3 = 19 units/day.

Work completed by all three in **5 days** = 19 × 5 = 95 units.

**Remaining work** = 150 − 95 = 55 units.

Time taken by **C** to finish = 55 ÷ 3 = 55/3 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 55/3 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **A** = 15 days, **B** = 25 days, **C** = 50 days, and time they worked together = **5 days**.

**Formula Used:** Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 **A**
 15
 150 (LCM)
 10
 
 

 **B**
 25
 6
 
 

 **C**
 50
 3
 
 

⇒ Total efficiency of (**A** + **B** + **C**) = 10 + 6 + 3 = 19 units/day.

⇒ Work done by all three in **5 days** = 19 × 5 = 95 units.

⇒ **Remaining work** to be completed = Total Work − Work Done = 150 − 95 = 55 units.

⇒ Time taken by **C** alone to complete the **remaining work** = 55 ÷ 3 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 55/3 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the ratio of time taken by two people is x : y, then the ratio of their efficiency is y : x.

Pipes and Cisterns

The same LCM method applies. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency, while outlet (leakage) pipes have negative efficiency.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each person. If they work for the same duration, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

questions.question: A car is moving at a speed of 108 km/hr. What will be the speed of the car in m/s?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To convert speed from **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply the value by the factor **5/18**.

Speed = 108 × (5/18)

Speed = 6 × 5 = 30 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 30 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the car = 108 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

⇒ 1 kilometer = 1000 meters

⇒ 1 hour = 60 minutes = 3600 seconds

⇒ Conversion factor = 1000/3600 = 5/18

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea6b8a7e147d8c9eaf2fe87a9701ee78ebb08f382c638aebe82b0899eed403de.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed in m/s = Speed in km/hr × (1000/3600)

⇒ Speed = 108 × (5/18)

⇒ Speed = 108 ÷ 18 × 5

⇒ Speed = 6 × 5

⇒ Speed = 30 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 30 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed Conversion Rule

To convert **m/s** to **km/hr**, multiply the speed by **18/5**.

Average Speed Formula

When a body covers equal distances at speeds **x** and **y**, the average speed is **(2xy)/(x + y)**.

Relative Speed

If two objects move in the **same direction**, relative speed = **S₁ − S₂**. In **opposite directions**, relative speed = **S₁ + S₂**.

questions.question: Speed of a train is 54 km/hr. This train crosses a platform in 18 seconds. Length of the platform is double of the length of the train. What is the length (in metres) of the train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **speed** to m/s: 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s.

Ratio of **Train Length** : **Platform Length** = 1 : 2.

Total units of distance = 1 + 2 = 3 units.

Total distance = 15 m/s × 18 sec = 270 m.

1 unit (Train Length) = 270 ÷ 3 = 90 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 90 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Speed = 54 km/hr, Time = 18 sec, Platform = 2 × Train Length.

**Formula:** Total Distance = Length of Train + Length of Platform = Speed × Time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a48609be3f23ab067e038586f451da180a77d0864eb427059496a8b178718324.png] 

⇒ Speed in m/s = 54 × (5/18) = 15 m/s

⇒ Let **Length of the train** be L.

⇒ **Length of the platform** = 2L.

⇒ Total Distance = L + 2L = 3L.

⇒ 3L = 15 × 18

⇒ 3L = 270

⇒ L = 270 ÷ 3 = 90

**∴ The correct answer is 90 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/hr** to **m/s**, multiply by 5/18. To convert **m/s** to **km/hr**, multiply by 18/5.

Train Crossing Concepts

When a train crosses a **pole** or **stationary man**, distance = Length of train. When it crosses a **bridge** or **platform**, distance = Length of train + Length of bridge/platform.

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the **same direction**, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. For **opposite directions**, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.
